name: Cheese rolls — whole-spelt, baked, parsley & egg (upgraded stuffed rolls)

source.author: Adapted from the 2-ingredient cheese-dough stuffed rolls (Hebrew blog/IG)
source.notes: Fully-upgraded, dual-lens-optimized version of cheese_dough_stuffed_rolls, designed with the user across several iterations. Changes from the original: whole-spelt flour (not white self-rising), cottage-cheese dough, 1 egg + fresh parsley folded into the batter, filling swapped to 9% light yellow + a little Bulgarian, BAKED with egg wash + sesame instead of pan-fried, no added salt. Parsley replaces spinach (Lihi doesn't like spinach) — slightly less folate but adds vitamin C to aid iron absorption. Makes 9 rolls; macros PER ROLL. Egg counted as 1 in the dough + ~½ of a second as wash. Estimate.

serving_desc: 1 stuffed roll (~90 g baked) — recipe makes 9

ingredients.note: + baking powder makes it self-rising; softer/stickier than white — handle gently
spinach replacement — folate + iron + vitamin C; up to 1 cup for more
cheeses + baking powder bring enough sodium
kept per user; verify pasteurized (see her note)

steps: Mix the dough ingredients (spelt + baking powder, cottage, egg, parsley, herbs) just until uniform.
Divide into 9 pieces; flatten each into a round.
Place the 9% yellow + Bulgarian in the center, gather and pinch sealed into a ball; set seam-side down.
Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle sesame.
Bake at 190–200 °C for 18–22 min until golden and cooked through. Serve warm.

batch_totals.note: All 9 rolls, baked (no frying oil), incl. 1 dough egg + ~½ egg wash + ~5 g sesame. Vs the original fried white-flour version (per roll ~189 kcal / 7.5 g protein / 1 g fiber): +55% protein, ~3.4x fiber, ~25% less fat, lower sodium, and meaningful folate/iron/choline.

him.verdict: About the ceiling for a stuffed cheese BREAD and a genuine rotation-worthy upgrade: ~11.4 g protein per 176 kcal roll (~6.5 g protein per 100 kcal) with ~3.3 g fiber — more than triple the original — from the whole-spelt flour, cottage dough and egg. Baking instead of frying removes the added oil, and dropping the added salt plus using 9% cheese keeps sodium moderate. Still a bread (carb-forward), so it's a strong carb+protein portion rather than a pure protein source, but as breads go this is excellent for your cut.
flags: ~11.4 g protein / roll at 176 kcal (~6.5 g protein per 100 kcal)
baked, not fried — no added frying oil
moderate sodium (~247 mg/roll; no added salt)
whole-grain, with folate + iron + choline the original lacked
suggested_mods: Great as-is; pair with a salad/tomato for extra fiber + vitamin C
To push protein even higher, add a scoop of unflavored whey to the dough or bump the 9% cheese in the filling
Keep them ~90 g each for a clean one-roll logging unit

her_preconception.verdict: A strong preconception bread now. Whole spelt brings folate + iron (her top two nutrients), the egg adds choline (fetal brain development), and the parsley contributes more folate/iron plus vitamin C that boosts absorption of the spelt's iron. All cheeses pasteurized and fully baked. The one thing to confirm is the Bulgarian cheese (brined soft cheese): it's baked through here — considered safe when cooked — and most Israeli Bulgarit is pasteurized, but verify it or leave it out. Parsley was chosen over spinach per her preference; it holds the score at 9.
prenatal_highlights: folate + iron from whole spelt + parsley (her top preconception nutrients)
choline from the eggs; vitamin C from parsley aids iron absorption
calcium + protein from cottage + yellow cheese; fully baked

safety_advisories.note: Bulgarian cheese is a brined soft cheese — Listeria risk unless pasteurized. It's baked through here (considered safe cooked) and most Israeli Bulgarit is pasteurized; verify, or omit and use more 9% yellow.
safety_advisories.swap: verify pasteurized / cook through (as here), or replace with more 9% yellow cheese

suggested_mods: Serve with tomato/pepper for extra vitamin C to maximize iron absorption
Bump the parsley toward 1 cup for even more folate/iron if she likes the herby taste

adopted_note: Adopted 2026-09-25 as the definitive upgraded version of the stuffed cheese rolls (designed with the user across several iterations; supersedes the original cheese_dough_stuffed_rolls for actual use). Per roll (of 9): ~176 kcal, 11.4 g protein, 3.3 g fiber, ~247 mg sodium. him 8 / her 9. Standing spec: whole-spelt flour + baking powder, cottage dough, 1 egg + ½ cup parsley in the batter, filling 70 g of 9% yellow + 30 g Bulgarian, BAKED (egg+sesame) at 190-200 C ~18-22 min, no added salt. Parsley is the spinach replacement (Lihi's preference); serve with tomato/pepper for vitamin C to aid iron absorption.
cooking_guide: Mix the dough JUST until uniform — whole spelt has weaker gluten and turns tough/gummy if overworked. Stop as soon as it comes together. The cottage + egg + parsley make a soft, slightly sticky dough; rest it 10 min for easier shaping.
Divide into 9 even pieces. Flatten each into a round ~½ cm thick, a little thinner at the edges so the seal isn't bulky.

Put the grated 9% yellow + crumbled Bulgarian in the center; don't overfill (cheese leaks). Gather the edges up over the filling and pinch firmly to seal into a closed ball. Set seam-side DOWN on parchment.
Brush all over with beaten egg (this gives the deep-golden, crisp surface) and sprinkle sesame.
Bake in a preheated oven at 190–200 °C (375–400 °F) for 18–22 min, until deep golden and cooked through in the center.
Rest 2–3 min on a rack (not a plate — trapped steam softens the crust). Serve warm while the cheese is melty.

Tips: whole spelt browns a touch faster — check at 18 min. Add a grating of garlic or chili flakes to the filling for more punch. Serve with sliced tomato or pepper — the vitamin C boosts absorption of the iron in the spelt + parsley.
